summary: Google DeepMind released Gemini Omni 1.1 Flash, an updated version of its video-generation model that adds scene extension, first/last-frame keyframe control, 4K upscaling, and a cheaper/faster 360p draft mode, available via Google AI Studio and the Agent Platform API.

mechanisms.reason: The model now retains and processes a longer window of prior video context per generation step, increasing per-request memory/context load compared to the prior version.
mechanisms.quote: With Omni 1.1, the model can now analyze up to 10 seconds of prior context — a leap from previous models that only referenced the final second.

mechanisms.reason: Cheaper, faster draft generation is explicitly positioned to encourage generating multiple variations per task, increasing the number of inference calls per creative workflow.
mechanisms.quote: Creators already generate several videos before landing on the right one. The Draft Room makes that exploration cheap and structured: generate 3-4 draft variations in 360p, varying one thing at a time and compare them side by side.

practices.reason: Teams building video-generation products can now extend scenes further, control keyframes, upscale to 4K, and use a materially cheaper draft mode.
practices.quote: Omni now delivers studio-quality video production, including the ability to extend a scene, first and last frame interpolation, crisp 4K upscaling, faster prototyping, and more.

practices.reason: Switching to 360p generation for prototyping is a directly reproducible technique for cutting cost and latency on this API.
practices.quote: Generate lightweight previews in 360p resolution up to 60% faster* and at a third of the cost compared to Omni 1.1’s standard 720p resolution.

practices.reason: New API parameters (previous_interaction_id, response_format resolution) and a new enterprise access path require integration work for teams building on this model.
practices.quote: Enterprises can build with Omni 1.1 directly via Agent Platform API .
